title: Unauthenticated basket cookie enables arbitrary code execution
description: The basket cookie is attacker-controlled but is passed directly to pickle.loads without a signature or other authenticity check. A remote unauthenticated attacker can submit a crafted cookie and execute arbitrary Python code when any basket-reading endpoint is requested.
evidence: read_basket() base64-decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads(raw) at shopapi/basket.py:16-20; the cookie is created with plain pickle.dumps at lines 26-28 and is not authenticated.

category: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
title: Passwordless token refresh accepts unsigned JWT claims
description: The refresh endpoint disables signature verification and trusts the attacker-supplied sub claim. Anyone can construct an unsigned JWT containing another user's ID and obtain a valid signed access token for that account.
evidence: jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}) is used at line 101, then claims.get('sub') is loaded and passed to make_token() at lines 104-107 without validating the original token's signature, issuer, or audience.

title: Hard-coded JWT and webhook signing secret
description: The production configuration contains a fixed SECRET_KEY, and the webhook secret also has a known default. The fixed JWT secret permits token forgery, while the default webhook secret permits forged payment events whenever the environment variable is not set.
evidence: SECRET_KEY is hard-coded as 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d' at config.py:3 and is used to sign JWTs in shopapi/auth.py:27; WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to the publicly visible 'whsec-local' at config.py:8 and is used for webhook authentication at shopapi/payments.py:54-63.

category: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
title: Authenticated users can read other customers' orders
description: The order detail endpoint authenticates the caller but never verifies that the requested order belongs to that caller. Any logged-in customer who can guess an order ID can retrieve another customer's order contents, payment totals, delivery information, and refunds.
evidence: show_order() returns order_json(get_order(order_id)) at lines 46-49; get_order() queries only by order ID at lines 25-29, while the ownership check exists only in own_order() at lines 32-35 and is not used here.

title: Product search concatenates the query into SQL
description: The public search endpoint concatenates the q parameter into a SQL statement. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause or use UNION-based input to read unintended database values.
evidence: The SQL at lines 40-42 is built as '... name LIKE %' + q + '% ...' and executed without parameter binding.

title: Customer display names are injected into the admin review report query
description: A customer can choose an arbitrary display name, and the staff-only report embeds that value directly in SQL. A malicious customer can therefore inject SQL that executes when an administrator requests the customer's review report.
evidence: update_account() stores the user-controlled display_name at shopapi/auth.py:119-125, and reviews_by_customer() interpolates customer['display_name'] into the SQL f-string at shopapi/admin.py:77-81.

title: Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML
description: Review bodies are user-controlled but rendered with the safe filter. An attacker can submit HTML or script content in a review body; it is stored and executed for visitors to the product page.
evidence: Review body is inserted from request data at shopapi/products.py:82-91, then rendered with {{ r.body|safe }} at product.html:13. The author_name expression at line 14 remains autoescaped.

title: Approved image URLs can redirect the server to internal destinations
description: The endpoint validates only the initial hostname and DNS result, but requests.get follows redirects by default. An approved public image host can redirect the server to an internal or otherwise restricted URL, bypassing the allowlist and public-IP check.
evidence: check_url() validates the original URL at lines 28-35, while requests.get(url, timeout=10, stream=True) at line 50 follows redirects without validating each destination.

title: Payment status timeout is treated as a successful payment
description: A timeout contacting the payment provider is converted into status='paid'. Network failure therefore lets an order enter processing without confirmation that the customer paid, creating a direct payment bypass.
evidence: The Timeout handler explicitly sets status = 'paid' at lines 39-42, after which lines 43-45 mark the order processing and set paid_pence to total_pence.

category: CWE-345: Insufficient Validation of Data Authenticity
title: Webhook accepts an arbitrary payment amount
description: The webhook signature covers only the order ID, not the event status or amount. A validly signed paid event can set paid_pence to any attacker-selected value, including an amount unrelated to the order total, which can corrupt payment and refund accounting.
evidence: webhook_signature() hashes only str(order_id) at lines 53-55; the paid handler then assigns int(event.get('amount_pence', 0)) directly to paid_pence at lines 69-71 without checking it against order.total_pence or provider data.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashes use fast, unsalted SHA-256 rather than a password-specific KDF. If the database is obtained, passwords can be cracked cheaply with dictionary and GPU attacks, and identical passwords produce identical hashes.
evidence: hash_password() returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at lines 15-16, and that value is stored during registration at lines 77-78.

category: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
title: Request logging records credentials and other sensitive request bodies
description: Every POST, PUT, and PATCH request body is written to application logs. This includes login passwords, password reset data, bearer-token refresh requests, and potentially payment or personal data, exposing credentials to anyone with log access.
evidence: The before_request hook logs request.get_data(as_text=True)[:2000] for all mutating requests at lines 29-31, with no endpoint or field redaction.
